100k limits reset-clamp current below 35uA; TPS22918 ON input leakage leaves ample enable voltage.
USB absent clears latch; only RECOVERY_N presets it. Supervisor RUN output does not request recovery. Both asynchronous inputs may assert while button holds supervisor reset.
USB-C priority, keyboard connector fallback; 30k/10k sets nominal 4.0V switching threshold. Reverse-current blocking; no guaranteed 100mA input current limit.
CT=10nF gives about 26.6ms typical rise; host bulk and peripherals disconnected during recovery. QOD open. Shared 500mA PTC remains downstream.
5.5V-tolerant Schmitt input and Ioff avoid back-powering 3V3; full-swing output gives reliable recovery clear without diode-threshold assumptions.
3.07V supervisor; CT intentionally open for 20ms typical delayed release. RESET open drain; R12 pulls RUN high. MR is independent of RUN/recovery latch preset.

notes: Keyboard connector pin 4 remains a power input. USB-C automatically takes priority when present; U10 prevents source-to-source backfeed.
For PC recovery with Amiga off, hold RECOVERY while connecting USB-C, then release after 0.1 seconds. With USB already attached, press/release RECOVERY.
Recovery is hardware: RUN reset presets U9, Q2 asserts BOOTSEL, U7 selects service data, U11 turns off USB-A power and Q3 isolates Amiga signals.
USB-C can supply normal operation from an adequately rated 5V USB supply. A PC port is not guaranteed to power normal operation without USB enumeration.
Keyboard-only operation remains possible; the A4000 documented 100mA limit is the guaranteed budget, and r7/peripheral actual demand must be measured.
OLED centered; RM2 antenna faces left. All assembled components on top. Two independent 12MHz crystals.
Both USB-A ports share selected supply through a soft-start switch and one 500mA PTC; this is not 500mA per port.
Removing USB-C clears the recovery latch; press/release RECOVERY without USB-C to reboot normal firmware from keyboard power.
